extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, researchers, and students preparing Chicago-style citations for books and periodicals
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and recommended practices from The Chicago Manual of Style for citing books (print and electronic) and periodicals (journals, magazines, newspapers), including formatting, locators, online access, and special cases (multivolume works, no-date, forthcoming, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributed books — name to use
rubrics_metrics.description: For a book published by one company and distributed by another, the name on the title page should be used; the distributor’s name is best omitted unless essential to users of a bibliography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Willke, Helmut. Smart Governance... Distributed by University of Chicago Press. Wording on the title page such as 'Published by arrangement with...' may be included if of particular interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date—books (year only)
rubrics_metrics.description: For books, include only the year (not month or day) as the publication date; the date is found on the title page or copyright page and usually matches the copyright date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If two or more copyright dates appear, the most recent indicates publication date. For any edition other than the first, include both the edition and the date of that edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: New impressions and copyright renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not confuse the publication date with the date of a subsequent printing or a renewal of copyright; statements like '53rd impression' or 'Copyright renewed 1980' should be disregarded for publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For new editions (not impressions) see edition rules; for reprints see designated sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multivolume works spanning years
rubrics_metrics.description: When an entire multivolume, multiyear work is cited, give the range of dates; if the work is incomplete, give the date of the first volume followed by an en dash; if a single volume is cited, give only that volume's date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow punctuation rules for en dash (no space between en dash and following punctuation). See examples of multivolume citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No date of publication (n.d.)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the publication date cannot be ascertained, use the abbreviation 'n.d.' in place of the year; a guessed date may be supplied in brackets or added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example forms: 'Boston, n.d.' or 'Edinburgh, [1750?]' If no publisher/place/date can be determined, include the bibliographic location where a copy can be found to justify inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forthcoming publications
rubrics_metrics.description: When a book is under contract and already titled but date is unknown, use 'forthcoming' in place of the date; 'in press' is narrower (typeset/paginated) but Chicago recommends 'forthcoming' for any work under contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If page numbers are available they may be given. Books not under contract are treated as unpublished manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arabic vs roman numerals in locators
rubrics_metrics.description: Use arabic numerals wherever possible for volumes, chapters, and other divisions, regardless of how numerals appear in the original, except for pages numbered with roman numerals in the original (usually front matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occasional legal exceptions exist; examples provided in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing ranges of pages/locators
rubrics_metrics.description: Express ranges using first and last numbers rather than 'ff.' (e.g., '140–41' not '140f.'); use standard Chicago rules for ranges (see 9.61).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to nonconsecutive pages are separated by commas; for author-date style see separate section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'ff.' and 'passim.'
rubrics_metrics.description: Resort to 'ff.' only when no final number can usefully be given; prefer explicit end numbers. 'Passim' ('here and there') is discouraged unless it follows a stated range with more than three or four precise references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting: 'ff.' has no space before it and is followed by a period; 'passim' takes no period and neither is italicized. For indexes see index guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations for page, volume, etc.
rubrics_metrics.description: Common abbreviations are p. (pl.), pp., vol., pt., chap., bk., sec., n. (nn.), no., app., fig.; in citations these are usually lowercased and not italicized (except when part of an italicized title).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All listed abbreviations except for p. and n. form plurals by adding s. Unless following a period, all are lowercased.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to omit 'p.' and 'pp.'
rubrics_metrics.description: When a number or range clearly denotes pages in a book, 'p.' or 'pp.' may be omitted; add them only where ambiguity threatens, or retain them if the author has used them consistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Charlotte's Web, 75–76' but 'Complete Poems of Michelangelo, p. 89, lines 135–36' where 'p.' clarifies.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to omit 'vol.'
rubrics_metrics.description: If a volume number is followed immediately by a page number, neither 'vol.' nor 'p.'/'pp.' is needed; numbers are used separated by a colon with no space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The Complete Tales of Henry James, 10:122. A comma usually precedes the volume number except with periodicals and some classical references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page and chapter numbers in bibliographies
rubrics_metrics.description: Page numbers are usually unnecessary in bibliographies except when the cited piece is a part of a whole (e.g., chapter in an edited book); the total page count of a book is not included in source citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For book review headings and catalog entries different rules apply; see relevant sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signed signatures and early-book leaf/folio citation
rubrics_metrics.description: For books printed before 1800 without page numbers, cite signature symbol, leaf number within signature, and r/v (recto/verso), e.g., 'G6v' or ranges like 'G6r–7v.' For folios use leaf number plus r/v (e.g., 176r, 231v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no discernible numbers exist, pages can sometimes be counted and the result placed in square brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid abbreviations 'l.' and 'll.' because they can be confused with numerals; use 'line' or 'lines' or omit if context makes clear the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Ogden Nash, 'Song for Ditherers,' lines 1–4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing numbered notes (n. and nn.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes are cited with 'n.' for a single note and 'nn.' for multiple consecutive notes; if the cited note is the only footnote on a page use 'n' alone after the page number, otherwise add the note number(s) directly after the page number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 72n, 80n; 192n23, 199n14, 201nn16–17. No intervening space or punctuation is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing illustrations and tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'fig.' for figure if desired; other illustration types (table, map, plate) are spelled out. Include page number before the illustration number, separated by a comma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 167, table 4.4. For art in collections and stand-alone works see dedicated sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-books — indicate application or device
rubrics_metrics.description: Because e-book formats vary, indicate which format or the name of the application/device used to read or acquire the book (e.g., iBooks, Kindle, NOOK); if a file format (EPUB, PDF) is specified, include that plus the application/device if relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E-book info should be the last part of a full citation. If the e-book is a reprint of an earlier printed edition, include original publication details followed by e-book information. In notes, e-book info follows page or other locator information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page or location numbers in electronic formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflowable e-book formats often lack fixed pages; prefer citing chapter numbers, section headings, or other mileposts instead of page/location numbers. If location numbers are cited, include both the specific location and the total number of locations using the application's terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'loc. 444 of 3023, Kindle.' If publishers include page numbers that correspond to print, check and cite the printed version if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Books consulted online — URLs and DOIs
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing an online version of a book, add a URL (preferably DOI-based) at the end of the citation. The citation should otherwise follow standard book citation principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a suitable URL is not available (commercial databases), list the database name rather than a restricted URL. Examples show DOI-based chapter links and direct URLs to digitized scans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer scanned editions for older works online
rubrics_metrics.description: For out-of-copyright works freely available online, prefer scanned pages (which include original title and copyright pages) to reflowable text for authoritative citations and for enabling fixed-page citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples compare Project Gutenberg reflowable texts to Google Books scanned copies; scanned copies make fixed-page citations possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Books on CD-ROM and other fixed media
rubrics_metrics.description: For books on CD-ROM or other fixed media, indicate the medium after the publication facts and include any page or other locator information in a note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The Chicago Manual of Style, 15th ed..., CD-ROM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'periodicals' in citation context
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Periodical' refers to scholarly/professional journals, popular magazines, and newspapers; except for adding a URL or database name, citation of a periodical consulted online follows same form as print periodicals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some publishers may require access dates; see general electronic source guidelines. See separate subsections for journals, magazines, newspapers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to include in periodical citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations of periodicals require some or all of: full author name(s); title and subtitle of article or column; title of periodical; issue information (volume, issue number, date, etc.); page reference where appropriate; and for online resources, a URL or database name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For newspapers and most magazines include full date (month, day, year). For journals include volume and year plus month or issue number as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals versus magazines — which form to use
rubrics_metrics.description: A journal is scholarly/professional and normally cited by volume and date; a magazine is cited by date alone. If unsure, use journal form if the volume number is easily located, otherwise use magazine form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided for distinguishing and formatting journal and magazine citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic punctuation and order in periodical citations
rubrics_metrics.description: In notes, commas separate author; article title (in quotation marks); title of periodical (in italics); and URL or database name for online sources. In bibliographies, periods replace these commas. 'In' is not used between article title and journal title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punctuation relative to volume/issue and dates depends on periodical type. See examples in notes and bibliography styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal article title formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Article titles are set in roman type, usually capitalized headline-style, put in quotation marks, with title and subtitle separated by a colon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For shortened forms of article titles and additional title-related rules see cross-referenced sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal title formatting and abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal titles are italicized and capitalized headline-style and usually given in full (omitting an initial 'The' in notes and bibliographies). Retain initial articles in non-English titles. Chicago recommends full titles unless a publisher/discipline requires abbreviation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some disciplines (science/medicine) routinely abbreviate titles; follow discipline/publisher rules if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal volume, issue, and date formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Most journal citations include volume, issue number or month, and year. Volume follows the journal title (set in roman), issue number follows the volume separated by a comma and preceded by 'no.' The year (sometimes with month or season) appears in parentheses after volume and issue data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seasons are capitalized in citations. When a span of months or multiple issue numbers is present, follow the journal's usage (use en dash in published version). If a journal uses issue numbers only, a comma follows the journal title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forthcoming and preprint journal articles
rubrics_metrics.description: If an article has been accepted but not yet appeared use 'forthcoming' in place of year and page numbers. Articles not accepted are treated as unpublished manuscripts. Preprints (not peer-reviewed) are treated as unpublished material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an article is published online ahead of print, use the posted publication date; page numbers or volume/issue information may not yet be available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal page references and continuous publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: In notes cite only the specific page(s) concerned; bibliographies give first and last pages of an article. For journals with continuous publishing assigning unique article IDs, cite page numbers (if present) before the article ID in notes and omit page range in bibliography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show how to cite articles with eIDs (e0124310) and continuous publishing models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal articles consulted online — DOIs and URLs
rubrics_metrics.description: Add information about the online resource to the end of a citation; a DOI-based URL (https://doi.org/...) is preferable to a browser address bar URL. If no DOI is available, use the form of URL offered with the article; where a link is restricted, list the commercial database name instead of the URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For articles offered in more than one format (PDF/HTML) there is usually no need to specify which was cited. If consulted in print, do not include a URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access dates for journal articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Chicago does not require access dates for formally published electronic sources, but some publishers/disciplines may require them; when included, place the access date immediately before the URL (or database information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting: separated by commas in a note and periods in a bibliography entry. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation rules when page numbers follow volume/issue
rubrics_metrics.description: When page numbers immediately follow a volume number separated only by a colon (shortened citation), no space follows the colon. When parenthetical information intervenes, a space follows the colon. If page number follows an issue number use a comma, not a colon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Social Networks 14:213–29' vs 'Critical Inquiry 1, no. 3 (Winter 1975): 479–96' and 'Diogenes, no. 25, 84–117.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal special issues and supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: A special issue (theme issue) carries normal volume and issue numbers and may have an editor and title; cite articles within it as usual or cite the special issue as a whole. A supplement is numbered separately and may have its own title and author/editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided for citing articles within special issues and whole special-issue citations; supplement citation examples include separate numbering (e.g., no. S1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Articles published in installments
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles published in parts over two or more issues may be listed separately or in the same entry depending on whether the part or the whole is cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show when to list parts separately (pt. 1, pt. 2) or to combine into one entry listing both issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article appearing in two publications
rubrics_metrics.description: When a work appears in two formats (e.g., journal and later in a book), cite the version actually consulted; if relevant to readers, annotate the citation to indicate the previous or alternate publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example annotations: 'Previously published as...' or 'A slightly revised version appears in Book Title...'

rubrics_metrics.name: Place where journal is published (add if ambiguous)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a journal might be confused with another of similar title or might be unknown to bibliography users, add the place or institution where it is published in parentheses after the journal title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Victorian Poetry (West Virginia University) 13, no. 1 (1975): 47–60.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Translated or edited articles follow book rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A translated or edited journal article follows essentially the same style as a translated or edited book—include translator or editor information as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Arthur Q. Author, "Article Title," trans. Tim Z. Translator, Journal Title...' or 'Author, "Article Title." Edited by Edward A. Editor. Journal Title...'
